title: Accelerated Design Verification Coverage Closure Using Machine Learning
problem: Design verification of complex ICs is bottlenecked by constrained random verification generating stimulus that does not provide incremental coverage, wasting simulation time and delaying time-to-market.
motivation: As IC complexity increases, traditional constrained random verification becomes inefficient. Predicting which randomly generated stimulus will provide incremental coverage can accelerate verification closure and reduce overall verification time.
method: Machine learning model to predict whether randomly generated stimulus will provide incremental coverage. Stimulus is simulated only if ML model predicts incremental coverage contribution.
key_novelty: First application of ML to predict incremental coverage during random verification, filtering non-productive stimulus before simulation.
contributions: ML-based stimulus filtering for coverage-driven verification
Predictive model for incremental coverage estimation
limitations: Abstract only; no experimental results, speedup numbers, or coverage acceleration metrics provided. No details on ML model architecture or training data requirements.
